svg.title: Who authorized the agent to make that payment?
svg.desc: Chalkboard diagram inside the outline of the Orange Tomato mascot head. The authorization chain: a person sets the boundary (budget, merchant scope, expiry, card type), chooses oversight (confirm every payment, approve above a threshold, or pre-approved scope), the agent acts, limits are enforced at authorization and anything outside is declined before money moves, and the executed payment is recorded naming the agent and the user. Outside the proof: merchants may decline unknown agents, the model provider sees data the agent reads, dispute and reversal mechanics are not public, and a misconfigured limit still binds as configured.

g.text: what the chain establishes — and what it doesn't
merchant tools may decline unknown agents
model provider sees data you read
Boundaries are human-set; agents cannot raise their own.
No independent audit · disputes not public
